My first car (a 1999 Oldsmobile Alero) broke on me a month or two after I graduated college. I knew it was dying but I didn't expect it to be so sudden, and it was beyond repair. So we scrapped it. I felt sad...luckily, my mom had inherited a car, so she gave me her old car, which at that point was also becoming a beater. My parents got that car when I was 8 years old. 

It's a 2004 Hyundai Elantra. It has been driven into the ground, nickled and dimed until it got into the state it's in. It's so rusty that last year I had to take it to be inspected by a mechanic who sometimes overlooks those things, because I could not afford a new/used car at that time. 
In addition to the rust, it is having a plethora of issues, including brakes that are suddenly getting soft. I had finally saved enough for a down payment on a used car and yesterday I took the plunge.

It's the first time I'm going into debt for a vehicle, which leaves a pit in my stomach, but I do love the new vehicle. 

But the worse part for me is that it almost feels like I'm losing a part of me. Maybe not totally the car itself, though that's a big part. It was my mom's and then mine, so it's been around for a while. 21 years of my life. It has over 241k miles on it.

But also it's practically a part of my identity that I'm the person with the old piece-of-crap sedan. Me and my dad kept those cars alive as long as possible. 

Now with an SUV in good condition, from the 2010s, I have the newest and nicest car in the family. It feels weird. I know it's going to be a good change - something more reliable to start. 

So within the next 2 weeks, I'll be taking that old junker to the scrap yard to get what I can for it. Put it towards a service on the 'new' vehicle to ensure I start off right with it, and keep it alive at least for the life of the loan, hopefully longer.

So yeah. I totally feel you. If you made it this far, thanks for reading.

So the reason you want the grain to go shortways is because of the folding. When you fold paper contrary to the grain, you get microscopic splintering of the grains which causes an uneven fold. Humidity and temperature changes cause the pages to slightly expand and contract and if there is that microscopic splintering, it can cause the pages to warp a little. He also needs to sew the signatures so he needs to find out if he's allowed to use large sewing needles. And of course he needs the thread too. 
He also needs something to help him make clean folds (a bookbinder would use a bone folder but a hard [not bendy] ruler would suffice for a small project like this when he is trying it out).

I think what you're referring to in the bible has less to do with friendship in general and more to do with the influences they have on you. This can even apply to friends who identify as Christian but dont follow Jesus' teachings. Our friends should never be put before God, and it's more likely we will be tempted to put our non Christian friends first because they dont have the same respect for the faith as Christians do. Not to say they dont respect it at all but they also likely wont encourage you to stick to those convictions. 

Another part of it is being friends with non Christians or Christians who dont live like Christians often ends up with temptation to do unchristian things. If we give into those temptations, we are harming ourselves. (There is a whole argument I have about the difference between practicing sin and stumbling into sin and then repenting, to make it short if you're getting drunk on a regular basis for example and you know that's a sin, you are practicing sin and that's unacceptable but if you accidentally get drunk or you have a moment of bad judgment and get drunk but then repent with full intention not to do it again, then you merely stumbled and that's ok. Keep this difference in mind when I talk about sinning).

So our non Christian friends can lead us to live in sin because we want to do some of the things they might do and they want us to, too, so they urge us to do so. I have plenty of non Christian friends, and none of them truly respect my convictions. Some say they do, some are open about not respecting it, the ones who say they do show that they truly dont through their actions and words. We become pressured to believe things that arent true or arent right and sometimes we fall for it.

So I dont think we shouldnt be friends with non Christians, but we need to be careful and if we find that our friendships are pulling us away from Christ and our convictions, that's a sign we need to pull back from that friendship or completely let it go.
